summary: Hanna Wałkówska was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau from circa 1945 to 1950 under Ludwik Skurzak. She subsequently held a post at the University of Breslau from circa 1950 to 1991.

Hannah Gould specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Oxford, later holding posts at Monash University, St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne, and the University of Melbourne.

Hannes Sköld was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Gothenburg and Lund University. He later served at Lund University as Docent of Slavonic Languages in 1920 and Docent of Comparative IE Linguistics in 1926.

Hanns Oertel, a specialist in Indology and linguistics, earned his Ph.D. at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held positions at Yale, Harvard, the University of Basel, the University of Marburg, and the University of Munich.

Hanns-Peter Schmidt was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf. He held positions at Deccan College, Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, University of Tübingen, and UCLA.

Hans Adolf Dietrich Hartmann worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Marburg, Berlin, and Dublin. After serving as Privatdozent at Berlin and Göttingen, he was Professor of Comparative IE Linguistics at the University of Hamburg from 1953 to 1978.

Hans Conon von der Gabelentz was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Göttingen between 1825 and 1828. He also founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Hans Delbrück was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1869 to 1873. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1883 to 1921 and Frederick William University Berlin in 1885.
Hans E. Kauffmann was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied under Robert von Heine-Geldern, at the University of Vienna, and completed his PhD at the University of Zurich by 1934.

Hans Frederik Hendriksen worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the University of Copenhagen under Poul Tuxen and Holger Pedersen, among others. He was a professor at Uppsala University (1947–1951) and the University of Copenhagen (1951–1983).

Hans Haas was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held posts at the German Theological High School, University of Tokyo, University of Jena, and University of Leipzig.

Hans Harder is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed his degrees at Heidelberg and Halle-Wittenberg, the latter under Rahul Peter Das. He served as an Assistent at Halle-Wittenberg from 1995 to 2007.

Hans Hartog, an Indologist, studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Bethel, and Munich before earning his Ph.D. at Marburg under Friedrich Heiler between 1937 and 1939. His teachers included Walther Wüst, Hanns Oertel, and Ferdinand Sommer.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder, an Iranian and religious studies scholar, earned his Ph.D. at Breslau. He held professorships at the University of Königsberg, University of Leipzig, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Göttingen.

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who earned graduate degrees from Northwestern and Yale, studying under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He held posts at Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Michigan, Chicago, and Munich.

Hans Jensen Jørgensen, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Marburg, Munich, and Kiel, earning his PhD at Kiel under Emil Sieg. From 1912 to 1919, he held a post at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin.

Hans Josef Nolte was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg between circa 1891 and 1894. He served as Director at Gymnasium Papenburg from 1904 to 1916.

Hans Kamstrup Vogt was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Oslo, Paris, and Yale, completing his Ph.D. at Oslo. He served as Professor of General Linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1946 to 1973.
Hans Karl Siegert was a linguist who studied at the University of Munich from circa 1935 to 1941 under the instruction of Walther Wüst.

Hans Krahe was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena under Ferdinand Sommer and Friedrich Karl Slotty. He held posts at the University of Jena, University of Würzburg, Heidelberg University, and the University of Tübingen.
